coverage.main: Read all six pages of arXiv 1802.04528v3 (10 January 2019): Sections 1-5, Algorithm 1, Figure 1 and references. The corpus lists only the arXiv record.
coverage.excluded_results: All results are white-box on the single MalConv detector whose embedding gradients generate the payload: evasion rates on the test set (99.21% L2, 98.83% L-infinity), spatial invariance (100% still misclassified after repositioning), file transferability (75% of payloads injected from file A to file B still evade the same detector), payload-size and entropy analyses. The 'transferability' is across files and positions on the same model, not across models; the authors list black-box attacks as future work.

f1.evidence: Detector accuracy (98% validation, 97% test) is reported as setup evidence; no cross-model evaluation exists.

f2.evidence: Attacks start from correctly classified malicious files, recorded as setup evidence; no transfer denominator exists.

f3.evidence: No source-to-target model transfer step exists.

f5.evidence: The payload is iterated in embedding space until misclassification, with a byte-length budget; no transfer result exists to which the field applies.

f6.evidence: No code is linked; with no transfer configuration this is neither a transfer recomputability success nor a failure.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded and hashed; no code, model or data release is linked.

bounds_exclusion.reason: Only same-model evasion rates are reported.

limitations: Cross-file payload reuse on the same detector is treated as cross-input, not cross-model, transfer, consistent with rank 49; an independent recoder could flag this boundary.
